definition: The three core goals of security: confidentiality, integrity and availability.
exampleSentence: Every security policy in our company is built around the CIA triad.

definition: The rule that only authorized people can read sensitive information.
exampleSentence: Doctors must protect patient confidentiality when they store records online.

definition: The guarantee that data has not been changed by anyone without permission.
exampleSentence: A checksum helps us prove the integrity of a file after the download.

definition: The goal of keeping systems and data ready for users whenever they need them.
exampleSentence: Cloud providers promise high availability so that customers can reach services all day.

definition: Anything that could cause harm to a system by using a weakness.
exampleSentence: The team wrote a report about each threat to the new payment system.

definition: The chance of damage when a threat meets a weakness, and how bad it would be.
exampleSentence: We accepted the risk because fixing the old server would cost too much.

definition: A piece of code or a method that takes advantage of a weakness.
exampleSentence: Attackers published an exploit only two days after the bug became public.

definition: The part of an attack that does the real harm after the exploit works.
exampleSentence: The payload downloaded a second program and started to encrypt the disk.

definition: All the points where an attacker can try to enter a system.
exampleSentence: Closing unused ports reduces the attack surface of every public server.

definition: A scoring system from 0 to 10 that shows how serious a weakness is.
exampleSentence: The bug received a CVSS score of 9.8, so we patched it immediately.

definition: A person or group that carries out or plans a cyber attack.
exampleSentence: The report names a known threat actor that targets banks in Europe.

definition: The path or method an attacker uses to reach a target.
exampleSentence: Email is still the most common attack vector for companies of any size.

definition: Anything valuable to a company that needs protection, such as data or servers.
exampleSentence: You cannot protect an asset if you do not know that it exists.

definition: The overall strength of an organization's defenses and its readiness to respond.
exampleSentence: After the audit, our security posture improved a lot in just six months.

definition: The process of finding risks and deciding how serious each one is.
exampleSentence: A full risk assessment is required before we move customer data to the cloud.

definition: The amount of risk an organization is willing to accept to reach its goals.
exampleSentence: The board defined a low risk appetite for anything that touches payment data.

definition: The risk that remains after all security controls have been applied.
exampleSentence: Some residual risk always remains, even when every control works as planned.

definition: A safeguard or rule that reduces risk, such as a lock or a log review.
exampleSentence: Each security control in the checklist has an owner and a review date.

definition: A record of who did what and when, used to review past activity.
exampleSentence: The audit trail showed that an old account had deleted the files at midnight.

definition: Proof that someone really performed an action and cannot deny it later.
exampleSentence: Digital signatures give non-repudiation, so the sender cannot deny the contract.

definition: The process of proving that a user is really who they claim to be.
exampleSentence: Strong authentication stops most attackers who only know a stolen username.

definition: The process of deciding what an authenticated user is allowed to do.
exampleSentence: Authorization rules decide which employees may open the payroll folder.

definition: The ability to trace every action back to a specific person or system.
exampleSentence: Shared admin accounts destroy accountability because nobody knows who made a change.

definition: The principle of giving users only the access they need for their job.
exampleSentence: We follow least privilege, so interns cannot read production databases.

definition: Using several layers of protection so that one failure does not break security.
exampleSentence: Defense in depth means that a stolen password alone is not enough to get in.

definition: Building security into a product from the first step, not adding it later.
exampleSentence: Security by design saved us weeks of rework before the product launched.

definition: The set of current threats and attack trends that affect an industry.
exampleSentence: The threat landscape changed quickly when attackers started to use AI tools.

definition: An event where private data is seen or stolen by an unauthorized person.
exampleSentence: The company paid a large fine after the data breach exposed customer emails.

definition: An accidental exposure of private data, often caused by a mistake.
exampleSentence: A public storage bucket caused a data leak that nobody noticed for months.

definition: A risk that comes from an employee or partner who already has access.
exampleSentence: Monitoring tools help us detect an insider threat before data leaves the building.

definition: A written document that explains the security rules everyone must follow.
exampleSentence: New employees must read the security policy during their first week at work.

definition: An automatic check that looks for known weaknesses in systems.
exampleSentence: The weekly vulnerability scan found three servers with outdated software.

definition: The ordered steps an attacker follows from first contact to final goal.
exampleSentence: Breaking one step of the attack chain can stop the whole operation.

definition: A clue, like a strange file or IP address, showing that a system was attacked.
exampleSentence: Each indicator of compromise is shared with partners through a secure feed.

definition: A wrong setting that leaves a system open to attack.
exampleSentence: A single misconfiguration in the firewall exposed the database to the internet.

definition: The state of being open to attack, for example a service reachable from the internet.
exampleSentence: The scan showed an exposure on port 22 that nobody had approved.

definition: A confirmed or suspected event that threatens the safety of data or systems.
exampleSentence: Every security incident must be reported to the response team within one hour.

definition: A route through connected systems that an attacker could follow to reach a valuable target.
exampleSentence: The diagram of the attack path showed how a printer could lead to the database.

definition: Simple daily habits that keep devices and accounts safe, like updating and using strong passwords.
exampleSentence: Good cyber hygiene prevents most of the attacks that reach ordinary employees.

definition: A number that combines the likelihood and impact of a risk to help rank it.
exampleSentence: The new database received a high risk score because it stores payment details.
